description_ru: Диалог трёх соседей по квартире, которые обсуждают счета, уборку и шум, и пытаются договориться без ссоры.
text:
Jess: Right, thanks for sitting down, everybody. I know nobody likes meetings, but I think we need one. Last week, I was told by the landlord that the heating bill was almost double the usual amount.
Omar: Double? That cannot be right. We hardly use the heating.
Kate: Well, somebody does. When I came home on Tuesday, my window was open, and the radiator was on full power.
Omar: That was me, I am afraid. I was cooking, and the kitchen was like a sauna. I did not think it would matter.
Jess: It does, though. The bill is divided into three, so a hundred pounds for one month is a lot to pay for a hot window.

Kate: Can I say something before we continue? I do not want this to turn into a trial. Last month, Omar said that he would look after the recycling, and I said that I would clean the bathroom, and honestly, I think both of us were sloppy.
Omar: Fair enough. I admit that the recycling bin has been overflowing for about ten days. I was planning to take it out on Sunday, but then my sister came to stay, and it slipped my mind.
Jess: That is exactly the point. Everybody means well, but nothing gets done unless it is written down. I suggest that we make a rota, and that every task is given to one person per week.
Kate: A rota sounds sensible, as long as it is not too strict. Last year, I lived in a flat where the schedule was displayed on the fridge, and the atmosphere was like a prison.

Omar: What would be on the list, then?
Jess: I have made a draft. Bins and recycling, kitchen floor, bathroom, shopping for shared items such as soap and toilet paper, and the monthly check of the fridge. That last one is mine, because I was the one who found a yoghurt from March.
Kate: Please, do not remind me. The smell was so terrible that I was convinced something had died in there.
Omar: In my defence, that yoghurt was not mine. I was told by a friend that it was a special kind that never goes off.
Jess: I do not think that is true, Omar. Let us move on before I lose my appetite.

Kate: There is one more thing I have been wondering about. The noise. I do not want to sound like a grumpy old woman, but on Thursday I was woken at two in the morning by music.
Omar: That was my cousin. He plays in a band, and he wanted to show me a new song. I told him to keep it down, but you know how musicians are.
Kate: I do not mind music, honestly. I mind not being asked. I have an early shift on Fridays, and a bad night makes me impossible for the rest of the day.
Omar: Understood. From now on, I will send you a message if anyone comes over after ten. And if you say no, I will tell them to leave, or I will lend them my headphones.
Jess: That sounds very reasonable. Could we also agree that quiet hours start at eleven during the week?

Kate: Agreed. Now, what about the money? Is it fair that we split everything equally? Jess, you work from home, so you use more electricity than Omar and me.
Jess: That is true, and I have been thinking about it. I would be happy to pay a little more, say five pounds extra per month, as long as it is not turned into a habit of blaming me for everything.
Omar: Nobody is blaming you. Besides, I have an idea. We could buy a cheap meter for the plugs, and then we would see exactly who is using what.
Kate: That is a clever solution. It would take the guesswork out of the argument, and I would not have to feel like a detective.
Jess: I will order one tonight. It costs about fifteen pounds, which is nothing compared with our heating bill.

Omar: May I raise another point? I have been told by my boss that I will be working abroad for three months, starting in January. I would like to keep my room, but I would not expect you to pay for it.
Jess: I see. So you would pay the rent but stay away?
Omar: Exactly. I could even find a temporary tenant, if you do not mind a stranger. Somebody quiet, preferably, who would not leave yoghurts in the fridge.
Kate: A stranger makes me nervous, but if we meet them first, I suppose it is fine. Let us decide that closer to the date.
Jess: Agreed. I will write that on the list as a question mark.

Kate: Is that everything? I would like to cook dinner before it gets late.
Jess: One last thing. I have to say that I am quite proud of us. Three months ago, this meeting would have ended with somebody slamming a door.
Omar: To be fair, the door is still loose from the last time.
Kate: Then let us add it to the rota. Whoever fixes the door gets a free dinner from the other two.
Omar: I accept the challenge. And as a gesture of goodwill, I will carry out the recycling right now, before the meeting is officially over.
Jess: Then this meeting is officially over. Thank you both, and please, close the window on your way out.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: Короткий и расслабленный звук, не как русское «и»; язык чуть ниже и дальше назад.
В конце слова кончик языка у дёсен, спинка оттянута назад: звук глубокий, не мягкое «ль».
Короткий звук, близкий к русскому «а»; не округляйте губы.
Присоединяйте конечный согласный к следующему гласному: «take-it», «turn-it».

questions.answer: The radiator was on full power while a window was open.

questions.question: What did the flatmates decide to make?
What was Kate's complaint about noise?
questions.answer: She was woken at two in the morning by music.
